open_loop_curve.reading_method: 300 dpi render, gridline and curve positions located with plot_grid_probe.py, grey curve = gain, black curve = phase

open_loop_curve.notes: Phase below the 0-deg axis above about 700 MHz (not plotted). Gain shows a shelf at about -2 to -3 dB from 500 to 800 MHz before dropping to about -9 dB at 1 GHz. Nothing plotted above 1 GHz.

DERIVED: equivalent to about 5-6 pF if read as a pure capacitance; it is the follower-input impedance including the test fixture.

pinout_notes: LFCSP (Fig. 1): 1 DISABLE, 2 FEEDBACK, 3 -IN, 4 +IN, 5 -VS, 6 NIC (no internal connection), 7 VOUT, 8 +VS. SOIC_EP (Fig. 2): 1 FEEDBACK, 2 -IN, 3 +IN, 4 -VS, 5 -VS, 6 VOUT, 7 +VS, 8 DISABLE. FEEDBACK is a dedicated secondary output placed next to -IN for the feedback network; it isolates capacitive load and package/bond-wire inductance of the main output from the loop (p13). No separate pin-function table.
tia_content_note: None. 'Optical electronics' is listed under Applications (p1) only; no transimpedance, photodiode or capacitive-feedback example or equation.
application_guidance: Unity gain needs 24.9 ohm at +IN; Table 4 recommended RF/RG for G = -1, +2, +5, +10 with noise: amplifier-only voltage noise 1, 2, 2, 5, 10 nV/rtHz and total 1.2, 2.7, 2.7, 6.5, 13.3 nV/rtHz (output-referred, Vs = +/-5 V, RL = 1 kohm); 24.9 ohm plus amplifier equal to the noise of a single 87 ohm resistor (p14). Noise model Fig. 48 (p15). Layout (p16-17): clear ground and power planes under the pins; one SOIC mounting pad can add 0.2 pF to ground; 0.1 uF bypass close to supply pins with electrolytic adjacent; a capacitor between the two supplies improves PSR and distortion; keep returns of input, output termination, bypass and RG close; solder the exposed paddle to ground. Capacitive load: Figs. 9-10 and 23-26, 10 ohm snubber.
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 12.6 V; differential input +/-1.2 V; differential input current +/-10 mA; storage -65 to +150 C; operating -40 to +125 C; lead 300 C (10 s); junction 150 C (p5 Table 3). Internal antiparallel diode pairs (two series diodes each) clamp the differential input to about +/-1.2 V; ESD diodes to both rails; protection diodes handle 10 mA, limit with a series resistor (p13).
other_notes: DISABLE pin (three-state): <2.4 V disables (+/-5 V: -5 V to +2.4 V); open = enabled; 4.3 V to 5 V = low input bias current mode (Table 7, p16). Turn-off 100 ns, turn-on 40 ns (+/-5 V) / 60 ns (+5 V); off isolation -48 dB at 1 MHz; DISABLE pin bias current 17/21 uA enabled, -35/-44 uA disabled (+/-5 V). Max power dissipation curve Fig. 4. Capacitive load peaking Fig. 10. Operating temperature -40 to +125 C.
inconsistencies: Supply range: Features say 5 V to 12 V; General Description and Tables 1/2 say 4.5 V to 12 V.

Bias-current cancellation: p1 'reduces input bias current by a factor of 60'; p16 'factor of 100'; p13 'less than 200 nA'; Features 'Low input bias current: 100 nA'; Table 1 gives -0.1 uA typ, -1 uA max (Table 2: -0.2 typ, -1.5 max).
Current-noise curve (Fig. 16) is measured only to 100 kHz and drawn flat to 100 MHz; the HF current noise is effectively unspecified.
HD2 at 5 MHz, 2 V p-p, G = +1, RL = 1 kohm: Fig. 17 reads about -96 dBc, Fig. 18 about -92 dBc (supply not printed on Fig. 18).
Table 1 lists 'Input Bias Current Drift 3 nA/C' while Table 2 lists 'Input Bias Offset Current Drift 2.5 nA/C' (different parameter names in the two tables).
Open-loop DC gain on Fig. 15 is about 80 dB because it is measured with RL = 100 ohm; Table 1 (RL = 1 kohm) gives 85 dB typ. Not a contradiction, but the curve load differs from the table load.
No GBW specification; closed-loop G x BW at G = +10 (370 MHz, RL = 1 kohm) is higher than the 20 dB/dec extrapolation of Fig. 15 (about 300 MHz, RL = 100 ohm).
